must_remember: Stokes' Law states that the viscous drag force on a spherical body is given by $F = 6 \pi \eta r v$.
Terminal velocity $v_t$ is directly proportional to the square of the radius ($r^2$) of the spherical body and the density difference $(\rho - \sigma)$.
Stokes' law is strictly valid only for purely laminar and creeping flow where the Reynolds number $Re < 0.1$.
The viscous drag force always acts in a direction opposite to the instantaneous relative velocity vector between the sphere and the fluid.
Terminal velocity is independent of the distance fallen and is achieved when the net force on the falling body becomes zero.

glossary.meaning: A fluid's internal resistance to flow, measured in Pa·s or kg/(m·s).
The constant maximum velocity reached by a body falling through a viscous medium when gravitational force balances buoyant and viscous forces.
A dimensionless number used to predict flow patterns in different fluid flow situations ($Re = \frac{2 \rho v r}{\eta}$). Heightened values signify turbulent flow.
The retarding force experienced by an object moving through a fluid medium due to shearing stresses.
